marketing.metaDescription: Experimental offline BLE mesh SOS prototype with an operator coordination panel. Does not replace 112.
marketing.not112Body: SOSMesh does not replace official 112 emergency services. This is an experimental emergency mesh network prototype.
marketing.heroLead: SOSMesh connects phones over Bluetooth Low Energy when cellular and internet are unavailable, forwards encrypted SOS packets through optional volunteer relays, and coordinates response on a real-time operator panel.
marketing.howIntro: From the phone through nearby relays to the coordination server and operator workspace.
marketing.howStep1Body: The mobile app stores SOS messages in an on-device outbox and state machine, then broadcasts over BLE to nearby devices—without requiring AI.
marketing.howStep2Body: A nearby relay device receives encrypted envelopes only; it cannot read SOS plaintext. The relay uploads ciphertext to the central API when internet is available.
marketing.howStep3Body: The central API validates signed packets, records delivery progress, and streams live updates to operators.
marketing.howStep4Body: Operators review cases on the web dashboard—map, tasks, teams, and audit. Opening a case is not the same as physical rescue.
marketing.featureOfflineBody: Device-to-device transfer works without cloud AI; messages stay in an encrypted on-device queue until a path to the server exists.
marketing.featureCryptoBody: Relays carry ciphertext envelopes only. Ingest rejects forbidden plaintext fields; relays must not see victim message content.
marketing.featureStatesBody: The timeline shows saved on device, received by a peer, accepted by the server, and viewed by an operator—each step has a distinct meaning.
marketing.featureWatchBody: Watch apps send SOS to the paired phone; there is no guarantee of standalone watch mesh or 24/7 background relay.
marketing.featurePanelBody: Web panel for cases, assignment tasks, teams, activity, and audit trails with accessibility-tested flows.
marketing.platformAndroid: Android phones with Bluetooth Low Energy mesh roles
marketing.platformWear: Wear OS companion sending SOS to the paired phone
marketing.platformIos: iOS phones with Core Bluetooth integration
marketing.platformWeb: Web operator workspace (sign in from this site)
marketing.securityBody1: Volunteer relays transport encrypted packets; they do not decrypt SOS content. Security headers and CSRF guards protect operator routes.
marketing.securityBody2: When a nearby device acknowledges receipt, that does not mean the server accepted the message or that an operator has read it.
marketing.securityBody3: AI, when enabled in backend builds, produces suggestions only; the operator UI labels drafts as unverified and AI does not make rescue or triage decisions.
marketing.limit112: SOSMesh does not replace official 112 / emergency services—call 112 first in Turkey.
marketing.limitApple: No mesh guarantee for iOS background, force-quit, or OEM power restrictions; documented scenarios only.
marketing.limitWatch: Watches depend on a paired phone; no independent watch mesh guarantee.
marketing.limitBle: Radio range and device policies vary; field validation requires real hardware tests, not emulators alone.
marketing.limitAi: Optional AI assistance is disabled unless explicitly enabled in your deployment; it never authorizes rescue actions.
marketing.limitPrototype: This repository ships an experimental prototype—not a certified emergency product.
marketing.faq1A: No. SOSMesh is experimental mesh communication. In a real emergency, call official services such as 112 first.
marketing.faq2Q: Can a relay read my SOS text?
marketing.faq2A: No. Relays forward encrypted envelopes; plaintext SOS fields are not shown on relay devices.
marketing.faq3Q: Does peer received mean an operator saw my SOS?
marketing.faq3A: No. Nearby receipt is one technical step. Operator review is tracked separately.
marketing.faq4Q: Does it work offline without AI?
marketing.faq4A: Yes. BLE store-and-forward and the on-device outbox operate without AI; cloud AI is an optional backend worker.
marketing.faq5A: No. Success depends on distance, environment, and device settings; treat untested paths as unproven.
marketing.footerNot112: SOSMesh does not replace official 112 emergency services.
marketing.footerNote: Experimental prototype—not a certified emergency service. Capabilities depend on your deployment and device support.

help.title: Help and support
help.intro: Operator panel help; end-user guides live under docs/user/ in the repo.
help.not112: SOSMesh does not replace official emergency services (112). Call 112 in an emergency.
help.offlineBody: SOS stays in an encrypted on-device queue; nearby BLE transfer runs without AI. Without internet there is no server/operator path.
help.permissionsBody: Bluetooth and (on Android) location for scanning are required. If denied, nearby transfer stops; the record remains on device.
help.relayBody: Off by default. When enabled you carry encrypted packets only and cannot read SOS plaintext. Peer ACK does not mean the server accepted the message or that an operator read it.
help.watchBody: Wear OS / watchOS sends SOS to the paired phone. No standalone watch mesh or 24/7 relay guarantee.
help.ackBody: The timeline shows technical stages: device → peer → server → operator viewed → case in progress. No guarantee of help or response.
help.failedBody: Call 112 first. Check Bluetooth/permissions; on iOS force-quit may stop mesh. Avoid duplicate SOS spam.
help.limitsBody: Apple background and force-quit limits; physical device tests NOT_TESTED; store/prod rollout BLOCKED_APPROVAL.
help.matrixBody: Android min API 26, iOS 17+, watch companion. See docs/user/platform-destek-matrisi.md
help.supportNote: Form submission awaits prod contact approval (BLOCKED_APPROVAL). Placeholder: DESTEK_ILETISIM_TBD — no real email or phone in the repo.
help.supportBlocked: Support channel not configured (BLOCKED_APPROVAL). Shown in this session only; not sent to a server.
